d056EligibilityAudit.whyIRanIt: Decision item 6 is the only place this act reaches beyond mechanics, and it is the claim most worth refuting.
d056EligibilityAudit.gate3: D-056 gate 3 requires the remainder be 'already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner'. After this act DR-G31 is exactly that, owner Product/CLI architecture, which is byte-identical to the live DR-104 row's own owner cell. Holds.
d056EligibilityAudit.gate2Attack: I attacked gate 2 directly. It forbids splitting when any remaining member is authoring rather than execution or measurement, and the proposed row's harness cell reads 'not authored'. If an unauthored harness counted as an authoring remainder, gate 2 would fail and the draft's claim would be overreach.
d056EligibilityAudit.gate2Refutation: The attack fails on D-056's own text and its own examples. The forbidden list enumerates authoring of fixtures, schemas, successors, actor-joins, missing design and still-UNDECIDED numbers; harness authoring is not among them. Decisively, D-056's motivating table lists DR-115 as eligible in kind with its leftover at DR-G01..G05, and I read those live rows: every one of DR-G01 through DR-G05 carries 'not authored' in its harness cell. An unauthored harness therefore cannot defeat gate 2 without unseating D-056's own worked example. The fixture bytes -- the thing gate 2 does care about -- are already authored and recorded at D-130.
d056EligibilityAudit.gate2Prior: D-162 recorded that gates 2 and 3 did not hold, because at that time no live DR-G* owned the remainder and the naming and harness successors were themselves unwritten authoring. Naming v2 and harness v2 have since been authored, and this act supplies the live owner. The flip is earned, not asserted.

Codex's Stage A audit reached the same scope, PASS_FOR_PROPOSED_GATES_2_AND_3_ONLY with both effects conditional on a later recording. This draft is that recording, so the conditional is discharged in the right order.
